newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM precious metals mostly weaker as yen rises.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM precious metals mostly weaker as yen rises.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metals futures ended sharply lower on Wednesday, except for palladium, extending early losses due to the yen's further rise against the dollar, traders said.
June platinum, which has no daily limit, tumbled by 97 yen per gram to close at 1,630 yen.
Other prices ranged from 25 yen to 47 yen down, with benchmark April ending 25 yen off at 1,373 yen.
"Private investors hunting for bargains in platinum futures at the opening, switched to selling later amid expectations Russia would resume PGM sales soon," one trader said.
Russia's platinum group metal export agency said in a statement earlier on Wednesday that it would resume exports at the "nearest" possible time.

Although trade in TOCOM platinum futures was buoyant the spot market was relatively quiet, as supply tightness and price fluctuations in the spot market made traders reluctant to arbitrage trade, they said.
Palladium futures, excluding spot June, were resilient despite of the yen's gains due to support from tight near-term supplies and a large overhang of TOCOM short positions.
June tumbled by 50 yen per gram to 800 yen.
Gold futures were lower, with benchmark April ending off 24 yen at 1,219 yen.
"The yen's sharp appreciation against the dollar caught local investors off guard, and prompted them to liquidate their longs," one trader said.
Spot gold was quoted at $343.10/60 per ounce at 0819 GMT, against $343.70/344.20 in New York on Tuesday.

In the physical market, the wide spread between gold and platinum caused investors to buy gold and sell platinum to take profits. Benchmark April silver ended 2.2 yen per 10 grams weaker at 173.2 yen. --Tokyo Commodities Desk
